# Jobs

18 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 10 standard (1 credit), 4 advanced (5), 4 premium (10) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

Job listings across four boards in one shape: LinkedIn, Indeed, Bing, and Xing each get a keyword/location search plus single-listing detail, on the canonical Job / JobList schemas. Also LinkedIn organization-id resolution (feed the ids back into the LinkedIn search filters) and salary ranges by job title and country with title suggestions. Search endpoints are premium (10cr); detail is advanced (5cr); the salary and organization lookups are 1cr.

## GET /v1/jobs/ashby/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns every listed job on a company's Ashby job board, 100 per page: title, location, department (job.ext.job_function), employment type, workplace (job.remote), the published date, the full description as plain text, the job link and the apply link, and the salary range with its currency when the company shows compensation. job.ext.board is ashby and job.company.id is the board name. The total is the board's exact count. A board that does not exist answers 404.

**Use when** a company hires through Ashby (its jobs live on jobs.ashbyhq.com) and you want its whole open roster with pay, 100 jobs a page.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** page (native `page`) · 100/page · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/100) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `board` (optional, string) - The company's Ashby board name, the part after jobs.ashbyhq.com/ (for example openai). · e.g. `openai`
- `url` (optional, string) - A jobs.ashbyhq.com link instead of board.
- `page` (optional, integer, 1-1000) - Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `board`, `url`.

**Response** `JobList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ job }` ([full schema](schemas/JobList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `job.title` | Job title. |
| `job.id` | The job's id on its source. |
| `job.url` | URL of the posting. |
| `job.company.id` | The employer's id on the job source. |
| `job.company.name` | Employer name. |
| `job.apply_url` | Where to apply. |

+27 more (types in the full schema): `job` {description, employment_type, experience_level, listed_at, location, remote}; `job.ext` {accepting_applications, applicant_count, apply_options, board, company_logo_url, country_code, industries, is_promote, job_function, job_provider, linkedin_company_name, posted_label, salary_currency} (+8 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/ashby/search" \
  --data-urlencode "board=openai" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/jobs/bing/search - 10 credits (premium)

Returns aggregated job listings from Bing matching a keyword and location, with optional date, employment type, and remote-only filters. Each row has title, company, location, and the original job board. List rows do not include an apply URL; pass an id to GET /v1/jobs/bing for the description and apply link. location is required on page 1.

**Use when** you want to search across boards in one call, then pass an id to bing for the description and apply URL. location is required on page 1.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 10 credits · typical 1.7-2.2 s

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Keywords, job title, or company name. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `location` (optional, string) - City or country. Required on page 1. · e.g. `United States`
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: week | day) - Maximum age: week or day. · e.g. `week`
- `employment_types` (optional, string) - Semicolon-separated: contractor, fulltime, parttime, temporary.
- `remote_only` (optional, boolean) - When true, only remote listings.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from the previous page.

- Provide at least one of `location`, `cursor`.

## GET /v1/jobs/google/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the job listings Google Jobs gathers from employers' sites and job boards for a query, 10 a page: title, the employer (job.company.name) and the site Google found the job on (job.ext.job_provider), location, description, employment type, the apply link (job.apply_url) and every site the job is listed on with its own apply link (job.ext.apply_options), the salary where Google shows one (job.ext.salary_min, salary_max, salary_currency, salary_interval), and how long ago it was posted in Google's words (job.ext.posted_label, for example 3 days ago; job.listed_at stays null because Google gives no date). Google's job attributes such as benefits come in job.ext.attributes. location narrows the search to a place in Google's own form, for example New York,New York,United States. Pass the returned cursor for the next page.

**Use when** you want to find jobs across many boards in one search, compare where a job is posted, or track openings for a role or company.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈10/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keywords, a job title or a company, for example software engineer. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `location` (optional, string) - A place in Google's form, for example New York,New York,United States or London,England,United Kingdom. · e.g. `New York,New York,United States`
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter country, for example us or gb (default us).
- `language` (optional, string) - Language of the listings, for example en or de (default en).
- `cursor` (optional, string) - The next_cursor from a previous page of the same search. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

| `job.title` | Job title. |
| `job.id` | The job's id on its source. |

| `job.company.id` | The employer's id on the job source. |
| `job.company.name` | Employer name. |
| `job.apply_url` | Where to apply. |

## GET /v1/jobs/greenhouse - 1 credit (standard)

Returns one job from a company's Greenhouse board with its full description as plain text, plus title, location, department, first published date and the job link. Send the job link as url, or board and id together (the id is the number in /jobs/<id> and in gh_jid=<id>). A job that has closed answers 404.

- `url` (optional, string) - A Greenhouse job link instead of board and id, for example https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/stripe/jobs/8172510.

- Provide at least one of `board`, `url`.

## GET /v1/jobs/indeed/search - 10 credits (premium)

Returns Indeed job listings matching a keyword, country, and optional city, sort, and radius, 20 a page by default and up to 100 with limit. Each row includes title, company, location, description, apply URL and the listing date, and where Indeed shows them the salary range with its interval (job.ext.salary_min, salary_max, salary_currency, salary_interval), the employment type, remote or hybrid work (job.remote, job.ext.workplace_types), the company's rating (job.ext.company_rating) and Indeed's job attributes such as skills and benefits (job.ext.attributes). Filter by how recently a job was posted, job type, workplace, salary, education, experience level and Indeed Apply. country_code is required on page 1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Page 2 with the cursor from page 1. Row ids work with GET /v1/jobs/indeed.

**Use when** you want to search Indeed in one country, narrowed by city, radius, posting age, job type, workplace, salary, education or experience, up to 100 a page. country_code is required on page 1.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 10 credits · typical 0.7-2.4 s

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Keywords, job title, or company name. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `location` (optional, string) - City or region within the country. · e.g. `San Francisco`
- `country_code` (optional, string) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example us, de, kr). · e.g. `us`
- `sort_type` (optional, enum: relevance | date) - relevance (default) or date.
- `radius` (optional, integer, min 0) - Distance from location.
- `radius_type` (optional, enum: km | miles) - km (default) or miles.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque cursor from the previous page.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-100) - Jobs per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Indeed can return fewer.
- `posted_within_days` (optional, integer, 1-365) - Only jobs that appeared on Indeed within this many days, for example 1, 3, 7 or 14. Indeed applies it loosely, so check job.listed_at if you need a hard bound.
- `job_type` (optional, enum: fulltime | parttime | contract | temporary | internship | permanent | temp_to_hire | freelance) - One employment type: fulltime, parttime, contract, temporary, internship, permanent, temp_to_hire or freelance.
- `workplace` (optional, enum: remote | hybrid) - remote or hybrid.
- `salary_min` (optional, integer, min 1) - Lowest yearly base salary, in the market's currency.
- `salary_max` (optional, integer, min 1) - Highest yearly base salary, in the market's currency.
- `easy_apply` (optional, boolean) - Set true for jobs that take Indeed Apply.
- `education` (optional, enum: high_school | associate | bachelor | master | doctoral) - Education level: high_school, associate, bachelor, master or doctoral.
- `experience_level` (optional, enum: entry | mid | senior) - entry, mid or senior.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `cursor`.
- Provide at least one of `country_code`, `cursor`.

## GET /v1/jobs/levels/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns jobs from the Levels.fyi job board for a keyword, company or location, or all of them to browse: title, company (`job.company.name`, and its Levels.fyi slug in `job.company.id`), location, when it was posted, remote, hybrid or on-site work (`job.remote`, `job.ext.workplace_types`), the job link and the apply link. Where Levels.fyi shows pay, `job.ext.salary_min` and `salary_max` are the yearly base-pay range and `job.ext.total_compensation_min` and `total_compensation_max` the yearly total compensation range, in `job.ext.salary_currency` (US dollars); a job without pay has nulls. Filter by seniority, work arrangement, minimum total compensation and posting age, and sort by relevance, newest or total compensation. Levels.fyi groups jobs by company, so a page carries up to 15 jobs from each of 20 companies and its size varies; `total` is the Levels.fyi job count. Pass the returned cursor for the next page.

**Use when** pay matters: filter tech jobs by seniority, remote or hybrid work and minimum total compensation, or sort by total compensation.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** page (native `page`) · page size not measured · depth unknown

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Job title, keywords or company, for example data scientist. Leave it out to browse. · e.g. `data scientist`
- `company` (optional, string) - A company's Levels.fyi slug, for example google (from levels.fyi/companies/google).
- `location` (optional, string) - A Levels.fyi location slug, for example united-states or san-francisco-bay-area; not a free-text city name.
- `sort` (optional, enum: relevance | date_published | total_compensation) - relevance (default), date_published (newest first) or total_compensation (highest first).
- `levels` (optional, string) - Seniority as a comma list of internship, entry, mid_staff, principal, manager, director, executive.
- `work_arrangements` (optional, string) - A comma list of remote, hybrid, office.
- `min_total_compensation` (optional, integer, min 1) - Minimum yearly total compensation in US dollars. Levels.fyi compares its median, which can include its own estimate.
- `posted_within_days` (optional, integer, min 1) - Only jobs posted within this many days.
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number from 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

| `job.title` | Job title. |
| `job.id` | The job's id on its source. |
| `job.url` | URL of the posting. |
| `job.company.id` | The employer's id on the job source. |
| `job.company.name` | Employer name. |
| `job.apply_url` | Where to apply. |

+27 more (types in the full schema): `job` {description, employment_type, experience_level, listed_at, location, remote}; `job.ext` {accepting_applications, applicant_count, apply_options, board, company_logo_url, country_code, industries, is_promote, job_function, job_provider, linkedin_company_name, posted_label, salary_currency} (+8 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

## GET /v1/jobs/salary - 1 credit (standard)

Returns min, max, mean, and median pay for a job title in a country, broken out hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly, plus the local currency. Use GET /v1/jobs/salary/titles first when the title is uncertain.

**Use when** Use it after salary/titles when you have a known title and want the pay band for that country.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Job title, preferably one returned by salary/titles. · e.g. `software engineer`
- `country_code` (required) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. · e.g. `us`

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/jobs/salary" \
  --data-urlencode "query=software engineer" \
  --data-urlencode "country_code=us" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
